verses.text: Then the LORD told me, “Even if Moses and Samuel stood in front of me, my heart still wouldn’t turn toward these people. Send them out of my sight. Let them go!

When they ask, ‘Where are we supposed to go?’ tell them, ‘The LORD says, “Those headed for death, to death. Those headed for the sword, to the sword. Those headed for famine, to famine. Those headed for captivity, to captivity.”’
“I’ll send four kinds of destruction against them,” says the LORD. “The sword will kill, dogs will tear them apart, and the birds of the sky and animals of the earth will devour and destroy them.
I’ll have them tossed from one kingdom to another all over the earth because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem.
Who’s going to feel sorry for you, Jerusalem? Who’s going to grieve for you? Who’ll even stop to ask how you’re doing?
You rejected me,” says the LORD. “You kept turning backward. So I reached out my hand against you and destroyed you. I’m worn out from showing compassion.
I’ve scattered them with a winnowing fan at the gates of the land. I’ve taken away their children. I’ve destroyed my people. They wouldn’t turn from the way they lived.
They have more widows now than there are grains of sand by the sea. At midday I brought a destroyer against the mother of young men. Pain and terror came down on her all at once.

The woman who had seven children is fading. She’s breathed her last. Her sun went down while it was still daytime. She’s left ashamed and bewildered. I’ll hand whoever’s left over to the sword in front of their enemies,” says the LORD.
Oh, my mother, what misery that you gave birth to me! Everywhere I go, people fight and argue with me. I haven’t lent to anybody, and nobody’s lent to me, but every one of them curses me.
The LORD said, “I’ll definitely strengthen you for good. I’ll make your enemy come begging to you in a time of disaster and suffering.
Can anyone snap iron, especially iron from the north, or break bronze?
I’ll hand over your wealth and treasures as loot. They won’t pay a thing for it. That’s because of the sins you’ve committed all across your land.
I’ll send your wealth and treasures off with your enemies to a land you don’t know. My anger has lit a fire, and it’ll burn against you.”

LORD, you know what’s happening. Remember me, come to my aid, and bring justice on the people who are after me. You’re patient, but don’t let me be taken away. Remember I’ve put up with insults for your sake.
When I found your words, I ate them up. Your words made me glad deep down. I carry your name, LORD, God of Armies.
I didn’t sit around with the people laughing and celebrating. I sat alone under the weight of your hand, because you filled me with anger.
Why won’t this pain let up? Why’s my wound beyond healing? Are you really going to be like a stream that tricks me by drying up when I need it?

So the LORD says, “If you come back, I’ll bring you back to stand before me. If you draw out what’s precious from what’s vile, you’ll speak for me. They’ll come back to you, but you won’t go back to them.
I’ll make you a fortified bronze wall against these people. They’ll fight you, but they won’t beat you. I’m with you to save you and get you out,” says the LORD.
“I’ll pull you out of the grip of the wicked and buy you back from the grip of the ruthless.”
